visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a close-up pan across a collection of Nausicaä-themed figures, focusing on a silver, segmented Ohmu creature with multiple glowing teal eyes mounted on a wooden base. The background is a cluttered shelf with various toys and collectibles under bright indoor lighting. (2) A man with long, dark wavy hair and a black t-shirt appears, holding a smaller metallic Ohmu figure with red eyes close to his face in a selfie-style shot. (3) A close-up shows a hand holding two versions of the Ohmu—one with red eyes and one with teal—squeezing them as if they are articulated or rubbery. (4) The man returns to the frame, holding a large, soft green plush version of the Ohmu with bright blue eyes against his face, looking toward the camera. (5) The scene shifts to the packaging of a model kit, showing a 1/20 scale Nausicaä and Ohmu, followed by hands flipping through an instruction manual with detailed line drawings of the creature's internal structure. (6) The man holds a large brown envelope with a promotional poster image of Nausicaä, then proceeds to remove bubble wrap from a large, framed original-style sketch of the Ohmu. (7) The camera pans across the framed artwork, showing the detailed pencil-style texture of the creature and a Studio Ghibli logo at the bottom corner. (8) The man poses with the large framed sketch in his hands, smiling broadly at the camera in a brightly lit room filled with display cases of figures.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a cheerful, rhythmic melody of the Nausicaä theme, featuring a female voice singing 'la la la' in a high pitch over bright synthesizer chords. There are no vocals or distinct SFX in this phase. (2) A distinct rustling sound of paper and thin plastic is heard as the manual is being manipulated, which blends with the ongoing BGM which maintains a steady 120 BPM. (3) A more intense and crinkly sound of bubble wrap and heavy plastic tearing occurs as a frame is unpacked. The BGM remains dominant, with the percussive rustling events providing a tactile layer to the auditory experience. (4) The BGM continues to its natural resolution as the video ends, with the melodic vocal loop concluding alongside the visual of the person posing.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video is a collection showcase aimed at fans of Studio Ghibli's 'Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind.' It systematically displays various 'Ohmu' related items—from small metal figures and soft plushes to a technical model kit and a framed artwork—to express the creator's deep interest and pride in their specific character-focused collection.
